newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia pipeline has lost 133,000 bbl.oil this yr.
newsitem.headline: Colombia pipeline has lost 133,000 bbl.oil this yr.

text.p: Colombia's Cano Limon-Covenas pipeline, the second largest in the country, has been dynamited 41 times this year and 133,000 barrels of crude have been spilled, state-run oil company Ecopetrol said Friday.
All the attacks were attributed to leftist guerrillas of the Cuban-inspired National Liberation Army (ELN).
In 20 of the blasts the pipeline, which has a capacity to pump about 250,000 barrels per day, was dented. In the other attacks it was holed, the Ecopetrol statement said.
The company gave no estimate of the value of lost crude and the cost of repairs and the environmental clean-up.
The latest series of attacks occurred at the start of this month. Back-to-back blasts put the pipeline -- which serves Occidental Petroleum Corp's Cano Limon field -- out of action for 12 days.
The pipeline was dynamited 47 times last year with the loss of about 105,000 barrels of crude.
The 485-mile (780 km) Cano Limon-Covenas pipeline was the largest in the country until the completion of the 500-mile (800 km) Ocensa pipeline late last month.

Ocensa serves the Cusiana-Cupiagua field in Colombia's eastern plains and is due to be pumping about 450,000 barrels per day by the end of this month or early next, according to heads of British Petroleum Co Plc.
